source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Replace the need for initial nursing education because continuing competency is intended to serve as the nurse's primary professional training.","B":"Standardize every state's renewal rules because continuing competency requirements are federally identical for all licensed nurses.","C":"Support continued safe practice by helping nurses maintain current knowledge and skills as evidence, technology, and standards evolve.","D":"Eliminate employer responsibility for competency assessment because completion of continuing education proves competence in every clinical skill."}}
source_row.rationale: Continuing competency requirements (which may include continuing education, periodic skills validation, or other mechanisms depending on the state) are intended to help ensure nurses maintain current knowledge and skills throughout their career, supporting safe, competent, and up-to-date practice in a continually evolving healthcare field, rather than relying solely on initial education and licensure.
source_row.source_detail: NCSBN Continued Competence resource collection, including 'Toward a Standardized and Evidence-Based Continued Competence Assessment for Registered Nurses' and post-entry-level practice analyses, addressing maintenance of competence after licensure.
